description: PP.AP is a multidisciplinary team dedicated to transforming complex, overwhelming scientific data into breathtaking digital experiences. We believe that the universe's most fascinating stories, like comets flaring to life or asteroids drifting across star fields, should not be locked away in specialized research archives. Our mission is to build story-first, interactive platforms that make the wonders of space instantly accessible to anyone, from curious individuals to classroom students.
summary:
Developed by Team PP.AP for the NASA Space Apps Challenge (Planet X & SPHEREx), SPHEREx Sky is a browser-native 3D celestial observatory and time-domain analysis platform for NASA's 102-band infrared all-sky survey. 
Addressing the challenge of detecting faint moving and variable phenomena across multiple survey epochs, we integrated real calibrated NASA/IPAC IRSA Level 2 FITS observations for high-proper-motion stars and variables, including Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi B (brown dwarf binary), WISE 0855 (coldest sub-stellar brown dwarf), RW Aurigae (dust eclipse), and R Draconis (Mira variable), alongside an astrometric 450 AU candidate model for Planet X exhibiting annual trigonometric parallax (458.4″ shift). The platform features digital difference image subtraction (IB − IA), automated blink comparison, 6-band infrared spectrophotometry (D1–D6), an on-demand NASA IRSA WCS cutout pipeline, 20 classical constellations with 31 audio voiceovers, and an immersive WebXR VR observatory for Meta Quest headset with controller raycasting, hand pinch gestures, and spatial audio. 
SPHEREx Sky democratizes time-domain astrophysics, transforming complex multi-epoch infrared survey data into an intuitive, accessible research laboratory for scientists, students, and educators worldwide.
details:
What Does It Do and How Does It Work?

Developed by Team PP.AP, SPHEREx Sky is a browser-native 3D celestial observatory and time-domain analysis platform for NASA's SPHEREx mission. It transforms NASA's 102-band infrared all-sky survey into an interactive scientific laboratory accessible on web browsers, mobile devices, and Meta Quest VR headsets.

The platform works by projecting NASA/JPL-Caltech all-sky infrared survey maps onto an inverted 3D celestial sphere (R=500), blending near-infrared starlight (0.75–1.6 µm) and mid-infrared interstellar dust (2.4–5.0 µm). It integrates calibrated NASA/IPAC IRSA Level 2 FITS observations across sequential survey passes to track high proper motion stars, brown dwarf binaries, and variable stars, alongside a physical 450 AU candidate model for Planet X showing annual trigonometric parallax (458.4″ shift).

Benefits and Intended Impact

- Democratizing Time-Domain Astrophysics: Citizen scientists and students can inspect multi-epoch infrared data without complex desktop software (such as DS9).

- Automated Anomaly & Motion Detection: Features real-time digital difference image subtraction (IB - IA) to cancel static background stars and expose moving bodies, automated blink comparison, and 6-band infrared spectrophotometry (D1–D6).

- Immersive Learning: Meta Quest WebXR Virtual Reality observatory with spatial audio, controller rays, and hand-pinch tracking, accompanied by 31 educational audio voiceovers for constellations and landmarks.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software Used

- Frontend: React 18, TypeScript, Three.js (WebGL & WebXR shaders), GSAP (timelines & animations), Lenis smooth scrolling, Web Audio API.

- Backend & Pipeline: Python 3.11, Astropy, NumPy, Pillow, Requests (WCS reprojection and IRSA TAP obscore queries).

- Voice Conferencing: Node.js, Express, LiveKit WebRTC SDK.

- Testing & Deployment: Headless Playwright (18/18 WebXR automated tests), Docker, GitHub Actions (GitHub Pages), Render.com Cloud Web Service.

Creativity and Factors Considered

- Scientific Honesty: We strictly distinguish between real calibrated NASA IRSA Level 2 FITS observations (Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi B, WISE 0855, RW Aurigae, R Draconis) and the hypothetical Planet X model, clearly badging each dataset.

- Hybrid Cloud Architecture: Ultra-fast global static CDN on GitHub Pages (HTTPS for WebXR) paired with a containerized Python cloud backend on Render for live NASA IRSA TAP FITS cutouts.

- Universal Accessibility: Service Worker (sw.js) enabling 100% offline planetarium use, full keyboard navigation, and prefers-reduced-motion compliance.
